title: Policy body draft
description: Output contract for policy_body_author. This is an INTERMEDIATE artifact, not a provisionable spec: it carries prose and citation POINTERS, and code resolves the pointers against the obligation register to produce a policy_spec. Deliberately narrow — the agent emits nothing that code can compute (refs, titles, paragraph numbers) and nothing that must be exact (quotation text). UNVERIFIED: written before the first run.

ref.description: The obligation's ref, echoed. This is the join key back to the register — title, principle, paragraphs and quotation text are all resolved through it.

items.description: Plain text. No HTML, no markdown, no entities, no paragraph numbers — the assembly step adds all of that. A short paragraph here is usually a symptom of abstraction, which is the failure mode that produces an empty derived standard rather than a vague one.

body_paragraphs.description: The policy body. Critical Data Manager reads this and nothing else when deriving the standard's requirements.

from.description: Which of the obligation's own arrays to index into. `citations` takes citations[i]; `measurable_expectations` takes measurable_expectations[i].citation.

index.description: Zero-based, into THIS obligation's array. Bounds are not checkable by JSON Schema — the assembly step must refuse an out-of-range pointer rather than silently dropping the citation, or a policy loses its audit trail without anyone noticing.

cite.description: Pointers, never text. The whole design: the model chooses which quotation applies (judgement), code reproduces it exactly (an action that must be exact). A quotation cannot then be untraceable by construction rather than by instruction.
